title: Exact nonstationary heat-excess statistics in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model
abstract: arXiv:2611.31303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exact nonstationary large-deviation statistics remain scarce for interacting many-body systems. Here we employ the macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) to determine the complete long-time statistics of heat excess produced by an initially localized heat pulse in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model. We find a remarkable nonlocal canonical transformation which maps the weakly asymmetric MFT problem, including its initial and terminal conditions, onto the symmetric problem, previously solved exactly. The resulting rate function is an explicit nonlinear deformation of its symmetric counterpart. We also extend the solution to heat measured beyond an arbitrary observation point.
summary:
- Exact long‑time heat‑excess large‑deviation statistics obtained for the weakly asymmetric Kipnis–Marchioro–Presutti model.
- A nonlocal canonical transformation maps the asymmetric MFT problem to the solvable symmetric case, giving an explicit nonlinear rate function.
- The solution is extended to heat measured beyond any arbitrary observation point.

title: Condensates and Edge Effects in the Generalised Takayasu Model
abstract: arXiv:2611.31325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, in the 1D Takayasu Mass Model (MM) of diffusion-aggregation with input, large condensates and a novel power law were observed in simulations, and later characterised exactly. We extend these studies to the Takayasu model with generalised input, and provide a relation to translate the distribution function of the MM to any model with a space and time independent injection process. In the 1D Charge Model (CM) of a system of size $L$, where $q=+1$ and $-1$ charge monomers are injected with equal probability at each site in each time step, there is a power law distribution of cluster charge $P(q)\sim |q|^{-5/3}$. This distribution cuts off at $|q|\sim L^{3/2}$ in the steady state for long times $t\gg L^2$ and a large charge condensate forms with a net charge between $-\sqrt{Lt}$ and $\sqrt{Lt}$. A distance dependent distribution function is observed around the charge condensate and near open boundaries, both of which act like an edge in the system, analogous to the observations in the MM. The charge distribution measured at a distance $x$ from the edge transitions from the previously known CM bulk power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-5/3}$ for small clusters ($|q|< x^{3/2}$), to a novel power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-7/3}$ for larger clusters ($|q|>x^{3/2}$). In the 1D Pair Injection Model (PIM), where $+1$ and $-1$ charge monomers are injected simultaneously at adjacent sites, the power law distribution $P(q)\sim |q|^{-2}$ cuts off at $|q|\sim L$ in the steady state for long times, and no large growing condensate is formed. We still observe a distance dependent distribution measured from the largest clusters, or an open boundary, with a bulk power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-2}$ for small clusters ($|q|< x$), and an edge power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-3}$ for larger clusters ($|q >x$).
summary:
- Generalised Takayasu model with space‑time independent injection maps exactly to the original MM distribution.
- 1D Charge Model shows \(P(q)\sim|q|^{-5/3}\) up to \(|q|\sim L^{3/2}\); a condensate of net charge \(\pm\sqrt{Lt}\) forms.
- Near open boundaries the law shifts to \(P(q)\sim|q|^{-7/3}\) for \(|q|>x^{3/2}\); similar edge‑modified power laws appear in the Pair Injection

title: What time is it in Assembly Space? Cronin and Walker's "The Physics of Causation" fails elementary dimensional analysis (Comment on arXiv:2601.00515)
abstract: arXiv:2611.31339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cronin and Walker claim that causation is quantified by an ``assembly index'', a count of the steps needed to build an object. Remarkably, they equate ``continuous time (as measured by clocks)'' to a multiple of the index, which is a dimensionless number. Their argument treats one parameter as simultaneously a rate, a time interval, and a pure number, and provides no timescale to convert index to clock time. This dimensional incoherence betrays, at best, an ill-conceived and ill-formed theory, and fatally undermines two central claims. First, the exponential weighting at the heart of what they call the assembly equation can be obtained only by supplying a timescale, which they never do, or by recasting clock time as a dimensionless count of assembly steps. In the latter case, their ``derivation'' trivially reduces to Bernoulli's seventeenth-century compound-interest limit. Second, lacking rates or energy scales, their account cannot predict how quickly, or under what conditions, anything forms, and yet formation ``in finite time'' is their criterion for distinguishing spontaneous from ``selected'' objects. Assembly theory is thus incapable of addressing causation.
summary:
- Points out dimensional inconsistency in equating a dimensionless assembly index with continuous time.
- Shows that without a timescale the exponential weighting reduces to a trivial compound‑interest form and cannot predict formation rates.
- Concludes Assembly Theory cannot address causation because it lacks rates or energy scales.

title: Morphogenic necking of surfaces
authors: Farzan Vafa, Puskar Mondal, L. Mahadevan
abstract: arXiv:2611.31360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. For frozen morphogen profiles in simple axisymmetric examples, the gradient-driven route gives exact algebraic contraction, while the curvature-driven route gives local exponential contraction.
summary:
- Introduces an intrinsic framework linking morphogen patterns to surface geometry, balancing smoothing and deformation.
- Identifies two neck‑constriction mechanisms: gradient‑driven at steep morphogen fronts and curvature‑driven near localized peaks.
- Demonstrates exact algebraic contraction for gradient‑driven and local exponential contraction for curvature‑driven cases in axisymmetric models.

title: Band-Selective Coupling to Charge Density Wave Fluctuations in Kagome Superconductors AV3Sb5
authors: Peter C. Moen, T. G. H. Blank, C. Le, S. Smit, N. Heinsdorf, S. Sarkar, C. C. Au-Yeung, V. Zimmermann, J. Kraan, C. S. B. Pang, M. Tuniz, M. Bluschke, A. A. Haghighirad, I. Rajput, A. C. Salinas, S. Gorovikov, P. Dosanjh, J. I. Dadap, A. K. Mills, S. Zhdanovich, M. Michiardi, G. Levy, I. S. Elfimov, S. D. Wilson, M. Le Tacon, D. J. Jones, X. Wu, A. Damascelli
abstract: arXiv:2611.31362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The kagome superconductors AV3Sb5 (A=K, Rb, Cs) host multiband superconductivity (SC) within an unconventional charge density wave (CDW) parent phase, yet the relationship between the two remains unresolved. Through time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) experiments on CsV3Sb5 and KV3Sb5, we observe coherent band oscillations driven by coupling to a low-energy CDW amplitude mode at 3.1 THz. We find this coupling to be highly band-selective, differing by a factor of over 2 even between bands with dominant V-3d character. We reproduce these results with frozen-phonon density functional theory calculations, offering insight towards the relation between differing Fermi surface characters and our observed band selectivity. Furthermore, we observe differences in coupling channels between KV3Sb5 and CsV3Sb5. These results establish CDW amplitude mode fluctuations as a band-selective low-energy coupling channel that intimately contributes to the interplay between CDW and SC in the AV3Sb5 compounds.
summary:
- tr‑ARPES on CsV₃Sb₅/KV₃Sb₅ shows 1 THz CDW‑amplitude‑mode‑driven band oscillations.
- Coupling is highly band‑selective (×>2 difference) even among V‑3d bands, confirmed by frozen‑phonon DFT.
- Distinct coupling in K vs Cs compounds indicates CDW amplitude fluctuations are a band‑dependent link to superconductivity.

title: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions
abstract: arXiv:2611.31366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatially nonlocal symmetries need not imply nonlocal gauge dynamics. Nonlocal canonical transformations make certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions onsite while retaining sufficient Hamiltonian locality for gauging. Symmetry relocalization yields exact or emergent gauge locality in 1D, 2D, and 3D, subject to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies. In 1D, a Hamiltonian-preserving transformation exchanges onsite vector and nonlocal spectral axial charges of a half-filled chain, enabling local gauging of each and exposing their mixed anomaly. Bosonization identifies momentum-winding T-duality, with a parity-projected operator flowing to a noninvertible topological defect. A nonperturbative norm-resolvent bound proves emergent dynamical gauge locality at finite chemical potential, while a doubled Chern-insulator parent reveals the duality's bulk origin and superconducting extensions reveal hidden compact symmetries. In 2D, the square $\pi$-flux Majorana model shares the Kitaev honeycomb model's single Dirac fermion and odd Pfaffian parity but supports sharp and exponentially local compact charges, the latter with nontrivial Chern topology. Relocalization retains Schwartz locality for asymptotically local gauging, while AIII/AII parents clarify bulk charge origin and parity-anomaly inflow. Two flavors yield compact $U(2)$, a quaternionic invariant, and asymptotically local non-Abelian gauging. In 3D, an exact mixed vector-axial flux response is derived, while a distinct model supports an exponentially local vector $U(1)$ charge with strong quaternionic topology. A nonlocal map makes the charge and Kramers symmetry onsite while preserving exponential Hamiltonian locality. For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.
summary:
- Nonlocal lattice Dirac symmetries can be relocalized by canonical transformations, preserving Hamiltonian locality and enabling local gauging.

title: Tunneling signatures of the Lifshitz transition in a superconducting vortex
abstract: arXiv:2611.31371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon states bound to a vortex line in a clean type-II superconductor form one-dimensional minibands that disperse along the vortex. The lowest miniband is separated from the Fermi level by a minigap $E_0\sim\Delta^2/E_F$. A magnetic field shifts the minibands of the two spin projections in opposite directions. At the threshold field $B^*$ the Zeeman energy equals $E_0$. Estimates for FeSe place $B^*$ at a few tesla. The lowest miniband of one spin projection then crosses the Fermi level, and a spin-polarized one-dimensional Fermi sea forms inside the vortex core. We develop the theory of tunneling spectra across this Lifshitz transition. We solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations numerically in the quantum limit for all momenta along the vortex and compute the local density of states with thermal and instrumental broadening. The zero-bias conductance at the vortex center is absent below $B^*$. It has a maximum near $B^*$ with the inverse-square-root field dependence of a one-dimensional van Hove singularity and decreases at higher fields. The next miniband produces a second onset at a finite distance from the center. The zero-bias signal is carried by one spin projection at the center and by the opposite one in the surrounding ring. We then project the screened electron interaction onto the filled miniband. The resulting Luttinger parameter is close to unity, so the core hosts a weakly interacting one-dimensional Fermi gas. Its quasiparticles relax through three-particle collisions in analogy with thermalization in quantum wires and at quantum Hall edges. The corresponding relaxation rates are established analytically.
summary:
- Zeeman field \(B^*\sim\Delta^2/E_F\) drives a Lifshitz transition: the lowest vortex miniband crosses the Fermi level, creating a spin‑polarized 1D Fermi sea.
- Tunneling spectra show zero‑bias conductance absent below \(B^*\), peaking at \(B^*\) with a \(1/\sqrt{B-B^*}\) van Hove singularity, then falling; a second miniband onset appears farther from the core.
- Projected interactions give a Luttinger parameter ≈ 1, implying a weakly interacting 1D electron liquid inside the vortex core

title: Tunable first-order transitions and magnetic hysteresis in Bernal pentalayer graphene
authors: Wentian Zheng, Jiawei Hu, Yuxuan Yao, Fang Xie, Zihan Wang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Qimiao Si, Yonglong Xie
abstract: arXiv:2611.31376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In two-dimensional electron systems, strong Coulomb interactions can spontaneously lift flavor degeneracies such as spin and valley, producing first-order transitions with hysteretic switching of interest for memory devices. The subband degree of freedom in multiband systems may be viewed as a flavor that not only participates in such transitions but also enables control of the hysteretic behavior, as a displacement field can shift the energy difference between subbands. Here, we demonstrate this principle in Bernal-stacked pentalayer graphene, whose low-energy spectrum comprises a monolayer-like Dirac sub-band together with light and heavy bilayer-like sub-bands. Local compressibility measurements resolve a fully symmetry-broken Landau-level spectrum and a sequence of phase transitions that occur when Landau levels of different subbands cross, at which strong interactions redistribute the occupation among flavors. We show that these transitions exhibit hysteretic Hall responses in magnetic field, confirming their first-order character, and that the magnitude and sign of the hysteresis are tuned by the displacement field, as expected from the subband Landau-level ordering determined in compressibility measurements. Our work establishes the subband degree of freedom in multiband systems as a resource for engineering hysteretic switching, and highlights how local thermodynamic measurements can link microscopic insights to macroscopic responses in quantum materials.
summary:
- First‑order, hysteretic Landau‑level transitions observed in Bernal‑pentalayer graphene, driven by interaction‑induced flavor symmetry breaking.
- Local compressibility reveals subband‑dependent Landau‑level crossings; a displacement field tunes subband energies, controlling hysteresis magnitude and sign.
- Demonstrates subband degree of freedom as a tunable resource for hysteretic switching, linking microscopic thermodynamics to macroscopic Hall response.

title: Non-integer high harmonic generation from many-body nonadiabatic gating
authors: Mingyao Guo, Luting Wang, Murali Suganya, Biqiong Yu, Martin Greven, Sritharan Krishnamoorthi, Raman Sankar, Yao Wang, David Hsieh
abstract: arXiv:2611.31383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High harmonic generation (HHG) in solids typically produces a rigid frequency comb locked to exact integer multiples of the drive photon energy. In strongly correlated materials, however, the light field can dynamically transform the electronic state on the timescale of harmonic generation itself, potentially violating this rule. Here, we report giant blueshifted, non-integer HHG in a cuprate Mott insulator Sr$_2$CuO$_3$ produced by mid-infrared excitations. Concurrent transient reflectivity measurements and time-dependent exact-diagonalization simulations of a driven Hubbard model support a many-body temporal gating mechanism that suppresses light emission on the trailing edge of the pulse, thereby blueshifting radiated harmonics in the frequency domain. Our findings establish HHG emission energy as a sensitive probe of quantum many-body dynamics and pave the way for exploration and manipulation of correlated electronic phases of matter with strong-field spectroscopy.
summary:
- Giant blueshifted, non‑integer high harmonics observed in Sr₂CuO₃ under mid‑IR excitation, violating the usual integer‑multiple rule.
- Time‑resolved reflectivity and exact‑diagonalization of a driven Hubbard model show many‑body gating that suppresses trailing‑edge emission, producing the blueshift.
- Demonstrates HHG energy as a sensitive probe of quantum many‑body dynamics, opening routes to manipulate correlated electronic phases with strong‑field spectroscopy.

title: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals
authors: Andrew Osborne, Rhine Samajdar, Andrew A. Houck
abstract: arXiv:2611.31384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The celebrated Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.
summary:
- Graph topology in 1D quasiperiodic lattices yields critically or exponentially localized dispersive states coexisting with flat‑band, finitely supported eigenstates.
- Exactly solvable mobility edges arise solely from the graph structure, extending Aubry‑André‑Harper physics.
- Exact diagonalization shows on‑site interactions delocalize localized states, highlighting the joint role of magnetic interference and interactions in transport.

title: Origin of quadrupolar order in the 5d$^1$ double perovskite Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$
authors: Dario Fiore Mosca, Leonid V. Pourovskii
abstract: arXiv:2611.31395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite extensive experimental and theoretical studies of quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$, the microscopic origin and relative energy scales of the interactions driving it remain unresolved. In particular, the observed ferroic ordering of the $z^2$ quadrupole has remained difficult to explain, as the relative contributions of superexchange, classical quadrupole-quadrupole interactions, vibronic couplings, and virtual excitations to higher-energy levels have not been established quantitatively. Here, we determine all these interactions from first principles and solve the resulting microscopic Hamiltonian. The calculated ground state reproduces the experimentally observed quadrupolar order parameters and the associated structural distortions with quantitative accuracy. Disentangling the individual contributions, we find that ferroic $z^2$ order originates from a linear-quartic coupling, generated by virtual excitations to the $J_{\mathrm{eff}}$= 1/2 doublet and driven by vibronic interactions. Our results establish the hierarchy of microscopic interactions underlying quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ and provide a unified $ab \ initio$ description of its coupled electronic and lattice degrees of freedom.
summary:
- First‑principles calculation of superexchange, quadrupole–quadrupole, vibronic, and virtual‑excitation terms in Ba₂MgReO₆.
- Microscopic Hamiltonian reproduces the observed ferroic z² quadrupolar order and lattice distortions quantitatively.
- Ferroic z² order originates from a linear‑quartic coupling via virtual J_eff = ½ excitations, driven by vibronic interactions.

title: Ground state and thermal phase diagrams of the magnetized spin-$1/2$ XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice
authors: Owan Cho, Seungho Lee, Hyun-Yong Lee, SungBin Lee
abstract: arXiv:2611.31412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice in a magnetic field is a paradigmatic frustrated quantum magnet, yet its ground-state phase diagram at generic anisotropy and its thermal phase structure remain incompletely understood. Here, using infinite density-matrix renormalization group, infinite projected entangled-pair operator, and exponential tensor renormalization group methods, supported by exact diagonalization, we resolve both issues. At zero temperature, we map the phase diagram continuously from the Ising limit to the Heisenberg point and find that the nonclassical $\Psi$ supersolid is a stable phase just below saturation at all anisotropies studied: it borders the one-third-magnetization up-up-down plateau directly in the strongly easy-axis regime and the semiclassical $V$ phase toward the Heisenberg point. In the strongly easy-axis regime, we uncover an intrinsically finite-temperature bond-nematic phase above the zero-temperature plateau--$\Psi$ boundary, in which the three bond directions become spontaneously inequivalent without transverse spin coherence or three-sublattice order. A hard-core-boson mapping reveals its origin: once thermal fluctuations destroy phase coherence, the field-doped holes settle on domain walls of the local up-up-down order, which are stabilized by quantum kink delocalization and aligned by its $Z_3$ registry. Our results call for reexamining high-field states in triangular-lattice cobaltates such as Na$_2$BaCo(PO$_4$)$_2$ and K$_2$Co(SeO$_3$)$_2$.
summary:
- Ground‑state phase diagram mapped from Ising to Heisenberg limits, showing a stable Ψ supersolid below saturation for all anisotropies.
- Finite‑temperature study finds a bond‑nematic phase above the zero‑temperature plateau–Ψ boundary in the easy‑axis regime, with inequivalent bonds but no transverse spin order.
- Hard‑core boson mapping explains the nematic as thermally delocalized kink excitations aligning domain walls of up‑up‑down order via a Z₃ registry.

title: High-density correlation energy of the electron gas
authors: Miguel A. L. Marques, Paulo R. Pires, Stefano Pittalis
abstract: arXiv:2611.31426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The high-density expansion of the correlation energy per electron of the unpolarized three-dimensional electron gas, $\epsilon_c = A\ln r_s + B + C r_s\ln r_s + D r_s + \dots$, is used in many approximations to the correlation functional of density-functional theory. The coefficients $A$, $B$ and $C$ are known exactly. We revisit the three diagram classes used to estimate $D$, namely bare rings, rings with one first-order exchange insertion, and third-order diagrams with three distinct momentum transfers. Their sum is $-0.0077880(9)$ Ha per electron, compared with the earlier estimate of $-0.010$ Ha. The difference comes mainly from the coupling-constant weighting of the exchange rings in the calculation of Carr and Maradudin. At order $r_s^2$, seven contributions to the single-logarithm coefficient $E_1$ sum to $(3.653 \pm 0.010)\times 10^{-3}$ Ha per electron. The three long-wavelength contributions to the double-logarithm coefficient $E_2$ sum to $\alpha^2(36\pi^2 - 208\ln 2 - 221)/(192\pi^4) \approx -1.433\times 10^{-4}$ Ha per electron, where $\alpha = (4/9\pi)^{1/3}$. Available diffusion Monte Carlo energies at $r_s = 0.5$ cannot distinguish between the two estimates of $D$.
summary:
- Re‑evaluated the high‑density coefficient D for the 3D electron gas, obtaining D = –0077880(Ha / e⁻, lower than the earlier –010 Ha.
- Attributed the difference mainly to the coupling‑constant weighting of exchange‑ring diagrams used by Carr and Maradudin.
- Determined higher‑order terms: single‑log coefficient E₁ ≈ 653 × 10⁻³ Ha / e⁻ and double‑log

title: A fermionic framework for quantum machine learning benchmarks
authors: J\'er\'emie Gince, Ayana Sarkar, Stefanos Kourtis
abstract: arXiv:2611.31458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a framework for building and benchmarking scalable machine learning (ML) models based on simulating free-fermion systems. Our fermionic ML (FermiML) framework is (i) versatile enough to encompass kernel methods and neural networks, (ii) applicable to classification and regression, and (iii) scalable to real-world datasets. FermiML models are quantum circuits sharing the building blocks of most quantum ML (QML) models: (parameterized) qubit rotations and entangling gates. This allows us to build fermionic surrogates that mimic the architecture, and hence the quantum resources and inductive bias, of any QML model while remaining efficiently classically simulable. We thus benchmark QML models against close fermionic counterparts on equal footing and ascertain whether a purported QML gain truly stems from classically inaccessible resources or is an accidental side-effect. Across 31 configurations from five classification datasets, we benchmark quantum kitchen sinks (QKS), instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) and generic parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) models against fermionic surrogates. fQKS significantly outperforms QKS and is statistically indistinguishable from IQP and PQC; fPQC outperforms IQP and QKS and ties PQC in 28 configurations. We also introduce fermionic fidelity and Pfaffian covariance kernels for regression and establish QML baselines for this harder task. Finally, we introduce a fermionic energy-based classifier scalable to large text and image datasets, which outperforms prominent QML models on images, beats or closely trails them on text, and stays close to classical baselines throughout. Our results show that while performance depends sensitively on architecture, FermiML yields fermionic surrogates that challenge or outperform their unrestricted counterparts and fermionic QML models that match the scale of classical baselines on real-world datasets.
summary:
- Introduces FermiML, a classically simulable fermionic framework that reproduces the architecture of quantum ML models for scalable benchmarking.
- Benchmarks QML models (QKS, IQP, PQC) against fermionic surrogates on 31 configurations, showing fermionic versions often match or outperform the quantum counterparts, challenging claimed quantum advantages.
- Provides fermionic fidelity and Pfaffian covariance kernels for regression, establishing new QML baselines for harder tasks.

title: Strong Co-O exchange interaction in $P4/nmm$ KCoO$_2$ and its effect on spin wave and N\'eel temperature
authors: Ilteris K. Turan, Walter R. L. Lambrecht, Jerome Jackson
abstract: arXiv:2611.31504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The exchange interactions of a classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian in KCoO$_2$ in the $P4/nnm$ structure are calculated using a linear response approach, derived from the transverse spin susceptibility, integrated over atomic spheres using a projector proportional the local magnetization and including all atoms as magnetic atoms. The exchange interaction between Co and its apical O is found to be by far the largest interaction and ferromagnetic. Its effect on the N\'eel temperature and the spin wave spectrum are evaluated. The Co-O exchange is found to strongly enhance the critical temperature in the mean field approximation but not in the random phase approximation.
summary:
- Ferromagnetic Co–apical O exchange dominates in KCoO₂ (P4/nmm).
- Exchange constants derived from linear‑response transverse spin susceptibility.
- Co–O coupling boosts Néel temperature in mean‑field but not in RPA, altering spin‑wave spectrum.

title: Spin Hamiltonian, magnetic anisotropy and excitation spectrum in altermagnetic $\alpha$-MnTe from first principles
authors: Matteo Costa, Dario Fiore Mosca, Cesare Franchini, Leonid V. Pourovskii
abstract: arXiv:2611.31548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hexagonal altermagnet $\alpha$-MnTe combines a near-room-temperature collinear order with a strongly spin-split electronic structure, yet the microscopic origin of its easy-plane anisotropy, its zone-center magnon gap and its anomalously large magnetostriction have remained unexplained. We derive the complete low-energy magnetic Hamiltonian of $\alpha$-MnTe from first principles, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory with a force-theorem evaluation of the full anisotropic intersite exchange, single-ion terms and classical dipolar couplings. The isotropic exchange, including the altermagnetic splitting of the tenth-neighbor coupling, agrees with inelastic neutron scattering data. Contrary to the common single-ion picture, we find that the easy-plane anisotropy and the magnon gap at $\Gamma$ are governed by classical dipole-dipole interactions, which enhance the zone-center magnon splitting threefold leading to quantitative agreement with experiment, while the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term is irrelevant despite its size. The same Hamiltonian reproduces the chiral magnon splitting along antinodal directions, mirroring the electronic spin splitting, and quantitatively accounts for the giant magnetovolume coupling of $\alpha$-MnTe through the volume dependence of superexchange.
summary:
- Derived a complete first‑principles magnetic Hamiltonian for α‑MnTe that reproduces isotropic exchange and neutron‑scattering data.
- Showed that easy‑plane anisotropy and the Γ‑point magnon gap are dominated by classical dipole‑dipole interactions, with negligible Dzyaloshinskii‑Moriya contribution.
- Explained chiral magnon splitting and giant magnetostriction through volume‑dependent superexchange within the same Hamiltonian.

title: Adaptive ghost Gutzwiller dynamics of Hubbard model quenches across coupling strengths over extended times
abstract: arXiv:2611.31631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Following the real-time dynamics of correlated electrons to extended times, at all interaction strengths, remains an open challenge. We address it with an adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation (td-gGA). The method extends the Gutzwiller approximation by auxiliary ghost orbitals. It adds more of them whenever the correlations that build up during the dynamics exceed a threshold. This is computationally far more efficient than keeping their number fixed. As a demonstration we take the interaction quench of the half-filled Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. For this paradigmatic problem, numerically exact nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) serves as the reference. A previous td-gGA study with a fixed set of 6 ghost orbitals per spin largely reproduced the available DMFT data. It lacked, however, an error estimate that would support predictions beyond them. With up to 16 ghost orbitals per spin, adaptive td-gGA agrees with DMFT wherever DMFT data are available, from the weak-coupling prethermal regime to the strong-coupling collapse-and-revival regime. At strong coupling it remains converged up to three and a half times as long as the DMFT data. Near the crossover between the two regimes, the system relaxes to thermal values that agree with DMFT. Resolving the dynamics in the number of ghost orbitals shows how the sharp dynamical transition of the Gutzwiller approximation turns into this smooth crossover. In the extended time window at strong coupling, we observe that the oscillation frequency is renormalized as predicted by our second-order strong-coupling expansion. With its built-in error estimate, adaptive td-gGA offers a systematically improvable route to the extended-time dynamics of driven and multi-orbital correlated systems, especially when combined with tensor-network or quantum solvers for the embedding problem.
summary:
- Adaptive td‑gGA adds ghost orbitals as needed, enabling efficient long‑time dynamics of Hubbard quenches.
- Matches DMFT across weak‑to‑strong coupling, extending reliable simulation time by ~5× at strong coupling.
- Resolves smooth crossover from prethermal to collapse‑and‑revival regimes, turning the Gutzwiller sharp transition into continuous dynamics.

title: Universal spectrum of weakly coupled quantum critical Ising chains
authors: Hansen S. Wu, Ribhu K. Kaul
abstract: arXiv:2611.31655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spectrum of arrays of critical transverse field Ising chains perturbed by a weak inter-chain coupling in the scaling limit, using an exact diagonalization algorithm based on Hamiltonian truncation. As the number of chains is made large, we confirm the existence of excitations below the two particle continuum that can be identified with the celebrated Zamalodchikov $E_8$ theory with small corrections. In addition, we find a distinct $\psi$-particle, with mass $M_\mathrm{\psi}$ which is not contained in the $E_8$ theory. Its ratio to the lowest $E_8$ mass ($M_1$) is a universal number, which we have computed numerically to be $M_\mathrm{\psi}/M_1 = 1.819\cdots$ for a one dimensional array of critical chains. We present evidence that this new state fundamentally involves excitations on neighboring chains, explaining why it has no analogue in the single chain problem. Interestingly the $M_\mathrm{\psi}$ mass has a characteristic scaling dependence on detuning from the critical point that is qualitatively distinct from the $E_8$ masses, which can help identify it in spectroscopic experiments on easy-axis magnetic chain materials.
summary:
- Weak inter‑chain coupling in critical Ising chain arrays produces the \(E_8\) spectrum with small corrections.
- A new \(\psi\)-particle emerges, with universal mass ratio \(M_\psi/M_1 \approx 819\), absent in single chains.
- The \(\psi\) mass scales differently from \(E_8\) masses, providing a distinct spectroscopic signature.
